summary: Ran `ng update @angular/core@13 @angular/cli@13 --allow-dirty --force` from EFNgApp/EFNgApp/ClientApp on Node 16/npm 8, which bumped the @angular/* packages, CLI/build-angular, typescript, and applied the CLI's own migrations (IE polyfill removal, angular.json cleanup, .gitignore update, empty routerLink fix, TestBed teardown opt-out). npm 8's strict peer-dependency resolution then rejected plain `npm install` because @ngrx/* (still ^8.5.2, hop file lists 'none detected' for a bump this hop) declares a peer on @angular/core ^8; set `legacy-peer-deps=true` via `npm config set --location=project` (writes ClientApp/.npmrc) so install stays green until @ngrx gets its own major bump in a later hop. Separately, `npm run build` broke because src/main.ts (which Angular's own Ivy migration appended a `renderModule`/`renderModuleFactory` re-export to back in hop 01) pulled @angular/platform-server, and therefore its Node-only dependency chain, into the browser bundle; Angular 13's webpack 5 config no longer auto-polyfills Node core modules the way v12's did, so webpack failed resolving 'url'. Confirmed via Startup.cs that this app never actually calls UseSpaPrerendering (only UseAngularCliServer for dev), so the SSR export is unused scaffolding; fixed by moving it into a new src/main.server.ts and repointing the 'server' architect target (and tsconfig.server.json's files list) at it, which is the standard Angular Universal split and preserves both builds' output with no behavior change. Install and build now pass; test fails the exact same pre-existing way as baseline and every prior hop (angular.json's test target points at a nonexistent root-level styles.css instead of src/styles.css), so no new regression was introduced.
changes: Upgraded typescript from ~4.3.5 to ~4.6.4 (required peer range for @angular-devkit/build-angular 13)
Angular CLI migration: removed IE-only polyfill comments (classlist.js / web-animations-js) from src/polyfills.ts
Angular CLI migration: removed deprecated 'lint' architect targets (tslint builder) and other no-longer-valid options from angular.json

Angular core migration: fixed empty `[routerLink]=""` to `[routerLink]="[]"` in src/app/fetch-employee/fetch-employee.component.html (preserves prior 'link to current page' behavior now that empty routerLink disables the link in v13)
Angular core migration: opted src/test.ts out of the new default TestBed teardown behavior (`teardown: { destroyAfterEach: false }`) to keep existing test semantics

Manual fix: split the unused SSR renderModule/renderModuleFactory re-export out of src/main.ts into a new src/main.server.ts, and repointed angular.json's 'server' architect target and src/tsconfig.server.json's 'files' list at it, so the browser build no longer bundles @angular/platform-server (and its Node-only deps) and no longer needs Node core module polyfills under webpack 5

Manual fix: set legacy-peer-deps=true for this project (via `npm config set --location=project`, creating ClientApp/.npmrc) so `npm install` succeeds despite @ngrx/*@^8.5.2 and @nguniversal/module-map-ngfactory-loader@7.1.0 still declaring Angular 7/8 peer ranges
package-lock.json regenerated by npm as part of the update/install cycle
manual_followups: npm install still needs legacy-peer-deps (now set project-wide via ClientApp/.npmrc) because @ngrx/* (^8.5.2) and @nguniversal/module-map-ngfactory-loader@7.1.0 declare peers on @angular/core ^8/^7; this hop's detection again found no required bump for them (hop file lists 'none detected'). They should move to Angular-13-compatible majors in a later hop, at which point the .npmrc override can likely be removed.

`npm run build:ssr` (the 'server' architect target, used to produce the unused dist-server/ SSR bundle) now fails during its TypeScript check with pre-existing, unrelated ambient type conflicts in @types/jasmine and @types/ws (TS2430/TS2315) surfaced by the newer typescript 4.6.4. This is not one of the required checks (`npm run build` for the browser target passes) and SSR is not actually wired up in Startup.cs (no UseSpaPrerendering call), so it was left as-is; a future hop touching @types or Universal should look at it.

`npm run test` fails before any spec executes because angular.json's test architect target still points at `styles.css` at the ClientApp root instead of `src/styles.css`; this predates this hop (present since baseline) and was left as-is per the rule that pre-existing failures don't need fixing.
